surfaces.name: Luvus terminal UI and CLI (luvus binary; local, named-session and SSH-attached)
Luvus Web (optional browser client bridge, luvus web)
Programmatic surface (JSON control socket, CLI verbs, UHP 1.0 NDJSON, uhp access gateway)

claims.answer: Terminal-first. A single Rust binary runs the TUI on macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Linux (x86_64, arm64), FreeBSD amd64 and Windows x86_64; the CLI controls the same server; an optional Luvus Web bridge serves a browser client (read-only by default, --control opt-in) that works on phones behind a TLS tunnel; narrow SSH terminals get a touch layout. No native iOS/Android app and no editor extension.

desktop_os.answer: Release assets and docs ship the terminal UI for macOS (arm64, x86_64), Linux (x86_64, arm64), FreeBSD amd64 and Windows x86_64 (Windows Terminal); no desktop GUI window, no Windows ARM64 build.

mobile_apps.answer: Release asset list and docs contain no iOS or Android application; phones use the browser bridge or an SSH terminal app.

browser.answer: luvus web serves a browser client for live workspaces, terminals and agent titles from a loopback bridge with one-use pairing.

mobile_browser.answer: The browser client works on phones (touch controls dock, viewport-following terminal, file upload) but needs the user to run a trusted TLS tunnel because the bridge is loopback-only.

cli.answer: The luvus CLI exposes noun-verb commands (workspace, tab, pane, agent, task, automation, machine, web, uhp, doctor, update) over the local socket.

editor_extensions.answer: Bounded search of README, docs and repository tree (terms extension, vsix, marketplace, plugin for IDE) finds only a Codex plugin/skill and modules, not an IDE extension.

task_actions.answer: TUI and CLI start agents, send prompts, answer blocked prompts with agent keys and resume sessions; the browser can steer only with --control; DIFF review is read-only.

notifications.answer: Optional sound cues for done/blocked, sidebar state, silent notifications for red PR checks; no mobile push.

cross_device_continuity.answer: The server keeps sessions alive; any new client (TUI via --remote, SSH, browser pairing) attaches to the same live panes.

limitations: Not a desktop GUI app: the desktop client is a terminal UI.
Browser client needs a user-provided TLS tunnel for phone access; no native phone app.
No editor extension in the pinned release.

claims.answer: Luvus does not embed a harness: it runs many third-party agent CLIs untouched in terminal panes, detects them by process and screen, and adds resume, fork, usage and hooks per compiled-in adapter. Model-provider choice is entirely the agents' own. Custom agents can be taught via detection manifests.

harnesses.answer: Named supported agents: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, Codex, Arc Studio CLI, Antigravity CLI, Letta Code, opencode, Kimi, Grok, Hermes CLI, Pi, Oh My Pi, Muse Code, Fx, Cursor, Kilo Code, Devin, Gemini, Aider, Amp, Droid, Qwen, Kiro.

model_providers.answer: Luvus has no model-provider layer; each agent chooses its own provider and models. Mission Control reads usage and model names the agents record.

custom_adapters.answer: User manifests in ~/.luvus/manifests/<agent>.toml teach detection of a new agent; resume/fork/hook operations exist only for compiled-in adapters, and arbitrary executables can be started for ORCH tasks via --agent argv.

session_integration.answer: Agents run as ordinary processes in PTY panes (launched terminal command) with status read from process/screen; optional hooks and native-store readers give exact session ownership, resume and fork where an adapter implements them.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Panes of Claude Code, Codex, Copilot and others run side by side in one workspace and can prompt one another via agent prompt; ORCH workers can use different agents per task.

limitations: custom_adapters: User manifests in ~/.luvus/manifests/<agent>.toml teach detection of a new agent; resume/fork/hook operations exist only for compiled-in adapters, and arbitrary executables can be started for ORCH tasks via --agent argv.

session_integration: Agents run as ordinary processes in PTY panes (launched terminal command) with status read from process/screen; optional hooks and native-store readers give exact session ownership, resume and fork where an adapter implements them.

claims.answer: Luvus runs each agent with its own native login and credentials, so existing agent subscriptions or API keys work as the agent supports; Luvus holds no keys and sells no credits or models. Account switching and provider restrictions are the agents' concern.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Agents run untouched under the user's own login, so an installed agent's subscription route works; automation workers require the agent installed and authenticated for the server user.

api_accounts.answer: Agents launched in panes use whatever API key environment they are given; Luvus adds nothing between the agent and its provider.

vendor_credits.answer: Luvus is free local software with no vendor credits or hosted model service.

local_models.answer: Any agent that can use a local model works in a pane, but Luvus has no local-model integration of its own.

account_switching.answer: Bounded search of docs and agent adapters (terms account, profile switch, login) finds no account manager; credentials stay in each agent.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No Luvus account or login exists; luvus.dev has no account system.

provider_restrictions.answer: Third-party provider rules for running their CLIs unattended are not stated in Luvus docs.

limitations: Subscription/API support is inherited from each agent CLI; Luvus documents no per-plan details.
Provider terms on automation/third-party use are not captured.
claims.unknownReason: Provider policies are third-party documents outside the Luvus repository.

claims.answer: Install with a one-line script, Homebrew, deb/rpm, Nix or PowerShell, run luvus in a project folder and start any agent in a pane; luvus doctor checks git, gh and ssh. Non-Git directories work in the TUI and workspace-mode tasks; worktree features need Git; GitHub views need gh. SSH remote hosts can be set up from the TUI with managed binary install; no managed cloud.

first_task_setup.answer: Install, run luvus in a project, split a pane and start an agent (auto-detected); ORCH tasks add title/paths/gate and start with s. Agent login is manual.

no_git.answer: Workspaces are any folder; workspace-mode tasks run branchless in the existing directory; worktree mode reports not a git repo.

local_git_without_remote.answer: Git tab reads local commits, branches and status with git alone; worktrees and the merge gate need only a local repository.

hosted_git.answer: PRs, issues and checks need the gh CLI authenticated; without gh the tab degrades to a local viewer.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: luvus doctor checks git, gh and ssh; docs list the macOS Ctrl+Space conflict and SSH prerequisites.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: The project operates no hosted service and offers no managed cloud environment.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Remote Machine form or luvus machine add checks SSH, finds or installs a compatible Luvus binary with explicit approval, and saves the profile.

limitations: Worktree mode requires a Git repository; PR/issue views need an authenticated gh.
No managed-cloud option; remote setup assumes an SSH-reachable host.

claims.answer: Everything in the UI is also a CLI command and a typed UHP 1.0 method over a local JSON socket (owner-only), covering workspaces, panes, agents, tasks, automations, files, Git, DIFF and modules, with events streaming. A loopback uhp access gateway offers scoped, expiring remote access. The documented web client is an internal TypeScript package, not a published SDK. Luvus does not expose an MCP server.

cli.answer: luvus noun-verb CLI including task, lease, automation, agent, pane, workspace, machine, web and uhp commands with help all.

api.answer: Newline-delimited JSON control API (UHP 1.0) over a Unix socket or Windows named pipe, with schema, capabilities, snapshot and events discovery.

sdk.answer: The only TypeScript client (@luvus/uhp-client) is private, unpublished tooling for the bundled web app; no public SDK in the repository or docs.

mcp_server.answer: Bounded search of src, docs and web packages for mcp / Model Context Protocol finds only detection fixtures; Luvus exposes UHP/CLI and a skill, not an MCP server.

webhooks.answer: Luvus has no built-in inbound or outbound webhook. The documented example module examples/modules/agent-ping posts a webhook when an agent goes blocked or finishes; otherwise events are consumed through luvus events / UHP streams.

operations.answer: Create (task add, agent start), inspect (get/list/read/snapshot), steer (agent prompt/keys), stop (task release, pane close) and review (task done gate, DIFF notes) are all available via CLI/UHP.

authentication.answer: Local socket authority is the OS account (0700/0600); remote access uses paired, scoped, expiring tokens (read, control, orchestration scopes).

stability.answer: UHP is declared a stable 1.0 contract (luvus-uhp 1.0) with a conformance suite, while the project releases frequently and Automations are labeled BETA.

limitations: Automations and parts of the board are beta; no public SDK package.

claims.answer: Luvus is not an MCP client or a model runtime; MCP, skills and tool permissions are handled by each agent. Luvus itself is extended through modules (programs in any language with sidebar panels, panes, bar widgets, actions, worktree providers), themes, and an optional Luvus agent skill/Codex plugin.

mcp_client.answer: Bounded search for mcp/Model Context Protocol in src, docs and web packages finds no MCP client; agents inside panes use their own.

plugins.answer: Modules declared by luvus-module.toml add actions, events, settings, startup hooks, panes, docks and bar widgets; installable from GitHub repos.

custom_tools.answer: Modules can add actions and panes; Luvus offers no custom tool registry for agents beyond the CLI/UHP surface they can call.

instructions_import.answer: The optional luvus skill is copied into detected agent skill directories after luvus skill enable; Luvus does not import or manage other instruction files.

authentication.answer: Modules inherit the user's environment; install requires confirmation of declared commands; builds run with a scrubbed environment.

permission_scope.answer: Modules run with the user's OS authority after confirmation; scoped delegated tokens apply to UHP access, not to local modules.

integration_owner.answer: Luvus owns pane/terminal detection, modules and the skill; agents own MCP and tool connections.

limitations: No MCP client in Luvus itself; tool and MCP configuration is inherited from each agent.
Modules run local commands with user authority; no per-module permission model beyond install confirmation.

claims.answer: Pure Rust terminal UI (ratatui) in a single static binary; the optional browser client is a TypeScript web app bundled with the binary and served by the bridge. There is no Electron, Tauri, native desktop window or mobile app.

desktop_implementation.answer: Cargo.toml and docs show a Rust terminal application using ratatui; the desktop client is the terminal UI inside the user's terminal emulator.

mobile_implementation.answer: No mobile application exists; phones use the browser bridge (web app) or an SSH terminal.

hybrids.answer: Hybrid: Rust server with terminal UI client plus a bundled TypeScript web client (web/packages/app, web/bridge) over UHP.

implementation_evidence.answer: Pinned Cargo.toml, web package manifests and architecture docs.

claims.answer: Tasks are created locally on the ORCH board (title, paths, deps, gate, prompt) or via CLI; prompts are typed into agent panes or sent by Commander; no issue import from external trackers. Git tab lists GitHub issues and PRs read-only via gh. Automations trigger by time only.

local_creation.answer: ORCH board a / luvus task add create tasks with title, paths, dependencies, gate and prompt.

prompt_intake.answer: Prompts go into agent panes, Commander composer, or task prompt fields.

external_import.answer: Bounded search of docs and src/git for issue import found only a read-only Issues view; no import into tasks.

chat_git_triggers.answer: Docs state the automation beta is time-triggered; ORCH dependencies do not trigger automations; no push/PR/chat triggers.

authoritative_tracker.answer: The ORCH ledger (orch.json) is the only task record; GitHub issues are not linked to it.

stable_ids.answer: Task ids t1, t2 are sequential within a named session ledger; no cross-session or external IDs.

sync.answer: No synchronization with any external tracker exists in the pinned release.

supported_edits.answer: Tasks are editable until started; GitHub issue edits are not offered, only viewing.

external_roundtrips.answer: Any issue work beyond reading in the Git tab happens on GitHub itself.

limitations: No external tracker import or sync; GitHub issues are viewable only.
No chat or Git event triggers; automations are time-based (BETA).

claims.answer: A task carries a prompt/briefing, file-path globs, dependencies and an optional quality-gate command; the prompt is editable until the task starts and progress notes are appended; notes and output persist in orch.json. There are no acceptance-criteria objects, plan editors or revision history.

plans.answer: Task briefing (prompt, paths, deps) is a starting plan; no separate plan object.

acceptance_criteria.answer: The optional gate command acts as an executable acceptance check; no written criteria field.

editors.answer: luvus task update --prompt/--prompt-file edits a task until it starts; the TUI form edits fields at creation.

revisions.answer: Bounded search of src/orch and docs finds no prompt revision history; retry archives a bounded attempt summary only.

implementation_links.answer: A task records its branch, worktree and the integration commit after merge.

amendment.answer: Prompt and notes can be changed before start; after start only notes and status update.

restart_persistence.answer: Tasks, leases and notes persist in the session's orch.json across server restarts.

limitations: No formal plans, acceptance criteria or revision history; the gate command is the closest check.

claims.answer: Flat tasks with dependency edges: a task cannot start until dependencies are done (worktree-backed dependents wait for merged), path leases prevent overlapping assignment, and a retry creates a new attempt. No epics, parent/child nesting or task-to-epic growth.

epics.answer: Bounded search of docs and src/orch for epic/parent/child finds none.

hierarchy.answer: Tasks are a flat list with dependency edges; no nesting.

blockers.answer: Deps field lists blocking task ids; start is refused with deps not done.

readiness.answer: task.ready events and task next select ready work from the project queue.

enforcement.answer: task start validates dependencies and path lease before creating a worker; dependents wait for merged.

state_propagation.answer: Dependents become claimable when dependencies finish; no parent roll-up.

identity_retention.answer: A retried task keeps its id, notes and previous_attempts history.

workflow_constraints.answer: Lifecycle queued > claimed/running > done/review > merging > merged is fixed; manual or now start choice.

limitations: No epics or hierarchy; dependencies are a flat list.
Workflow is fixed to the task lifecycle.

claims.answer: Luvus does not own project memory: agents keep their own instructions, skills and memory. Luvus persists workspaces, layouts, optional pane screens and agent resume metadata, can resume or fork agent conversations with their context, and installs an optional luvus skill. AGENTS.md at repo root guides maintainers.

instructions.answer: No Luvus instruction store; the optional skill is the only Luvus-provided instruction content.

skills.answer: luvus skill enable copies a version-matched skill into detected agent skill directories.

project_docs.answer: Bounded search finds no project doc store; FILES dock previews Markdown/Mermaid read-only.

memory.answer: No cross-session or cross-harness memory; resume reopens an agent's own conversation.

scope.answer: Resume and fork scope is per agent conversation and project folder.

provenance.answer: No provenance tracking for context items.

correction.answer: No memory or context correction feature in Luvus.

deletion.answer: Hide (✕) removes a resumable entry from the list without touching the agent store; rm -rf ~/.luvus resets state.

freshness.answer: No stale-context controls beyond choosing resume vs fork vs new pane.

takeover_continuity.answer: Another client attaches to the same live panes; after server loss the next server rebuilds layout and resumes supported native sessions.

limitations: No Luvus-managed memory, project docs index or provenance/citation controls.

claims.answer: Luvus provides a global fuzzy finder over file names, workspace objects and retained terminal output and a Git-aware file tree, but no code indexing, embeddings, external knowledge or architecture checks; agents do their own retrieval. Clipboard images can be pasted into panes.

code_search.answer: Fuzzy finder searches file names/paths and retained output but not file contents.

indexing.answer: File path index per workspace honoring Git ignore; no content index.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Clipboard image paste and file upload from the web client into panes.

freshness.answer: Path index and file metadata refresh on bounded workers.

access_scope.answer: Finder reads names and paths under workspaces, not contents; skips .git.

api_retrieval.answer: luvus search and UHP expose the finder and pane output capture methods.

conflict_detection.answer: No architecture or API conflict detection.

review_enforcement.answer: DIFF review is read-only notes; no automated consistency enforcement.

limitations: No code-content search or index; file search is path-only.
No citation, conflict detection or review-time enforcement.

claims.answer: The ORCH board is a local task list with ids, titles, paths, dependencies, gates, prompts, notes, worker location and states, editable until start, with Manual vs Now start (an idea can be queued unstarted). It has no discussion, labels, assignment, priority, search, archive or project views beyond per-workspace project scoping.

create.answer: a on the board or luvus task add.

edit.answer: Prompt/paths editable until the task starts; later only notes and status.

discuss.answer: No discussion threads on tasks; notes are agent progress notes.

prioritize.answer: Bounded search finds no priority field; order is creation order.

assign.answer: Starting a task assigns an agent pane as worker; no human assignee field.

search.answer: Global finder does not index tasks; luvus task list lists them.

filter.answer: task list filters by workspace/project; TUI board shows all.

archive.answer: Retry archives a bounded attempt summary; no task archive.

reopen.answer: task retry reopens done/failed/review/blocked tasks as a new attempt.

project_epic_views.answer: Tasks are scoped per project (Git repository identity); no epic views.

idea_parking.answer: Manual start leaves a queued task without launching an agent.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Workers start only when s is pressed, task start runs, or Now is chosen.

task_session_separation.answer: Task owns a worker pane and attempt history; one active worker per task.

metadata.answer: Title, paths, deps, gate, prompt, mode, branch, worktree, output, notes, context usage.

durable_states.answer: Statuses persist in orch.json with events on every transition.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: No external tracker is integrated; teams needing tracking use their own.

limitations: No discussion, labels, priority, assignee, archive or epic views.
External tracker still needed for anything beyond the local list.

claims.answer: Agents in panes can run the same luvus task commands humans use: add, update, heartbeat with context usage, claim via task start/next, done and merge; leases, dependencies and notes are shared through the single ledger, and the board and events show changes live. No per-user attribution or permissions exist beyond OS user.

shared_ids.answer: Agents and humans use the same t-ids and lease records.

read.answer: task list/get and events are available to agents.

create.answer: luvus task add from any pane.

claim.answer: task next --start and task start claim queued work; the single-writer loop prevents double claims.

assign.answer: task start --agent chooses the agent worker.

state_changes.answer: done, merge, retry, release are CLI verbs.

children.answer: No child/subtask concept; agents can add dependent tasks.

results.answer: Notes, output and gate output stored on the task; heartbeat reports context use.

human_visibility.answer: Board and sidebar update live from the same ledger.

attribution.answer: Tasks show their worker pane; no author identity on edits.

permissions.answer: Local socket trusts the OS user; UHP tokens have read/control/orchestration scopes.

conflicts.answer: Single-writer event loop and lease conflicts prevent racing claims.

limitations: Writes are not attributed to a named human or agent identity beyond the worker pane; single OS-user trust model.

claims.answer: No living product specification, requirement store or spec drift check exists in the pinned release; DIFF notes and task prompts are per task.

persistent_requirements.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

human_edits.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

agent_edits.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

revisions.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

approvals.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

implementation_links.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

later_retrieval.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

drift_detection.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

review_integration.answer: Bounded search of docs and src (terms spec, requirement, specification) finds no living-spec feature.

claims.answer: Each pane is a real PTY owned by one detached server, so many agent panes and ORCH workers run concurrently across workspaces; the AGENTS sidebar, Mission Control and the board show blocked/working/done/idle states. The only documented bounds are bounded automation counts (256 definitions); no per-user concurrency quota.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Multiple panes and named-session servers run independently.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Several ORCH workers run in parallel in separate worktrees or task tabs; leases keep paths disjoint.

quotas.answer: Automation bounds (256 definitions, 2,048 run records, 32 KiB prompts); no concurrency quota.

observed_concurrency.answer: Maximum concurrency is not documented or measured by this catalog.

status_visibility.answer: Sidebar and Mission Control show blocked/working/done/idle with live updates.

limitations: quotas: Automation bounds (256 definitions, 2,048 run records, 32 KiB prompts); no concurrency quota.
observed_concurrency: Maximum concurrency is not documented or measured by this catalog.
claims.unknownReason: The catalog does not measure runtime concurrency; docs state no limit.

claims.answer: Humans or agents start tasks onto agent panes; leases give enforced exclusive path reservations within a project and dependency checks gate starts; task next picks queued ready work; automations queue at most one pending run. No named assignees or routing rules.

human_assignment.answer: A human starts a task onto an agent; no assignee field for people.

agent_assignment.answer: task start --agent and automation targets choose the agent.

claims.answer: task claimed/running states and the single-writer loop.

queues.answer: Queued tasks, task next, automation queue_one overlap policy.

routing.answer: Per-project queues; no skill or capacity routing.

duplicate_prevention.answer: Lease conflict rejects overlapping paths; automations key occurrences by definition and time.

ownership_enforcement.answer: Leases are enforced at start but do not stop agents writing outside declared paths in workspace mode.

limitations: No human assignees or routing rules; leases cover declared paths only and do not stop external writers.

claims.answer: Product-supplied delegation: one agent pane can start, name, prompt, wait for, read and send keys to other agent panes through luvus agent commands (any harness), with optional skill and = shorthand; ORCH lets a coordinator create worktree workers. Child identity is the pane/alias and results are read from retained output or tasks. Not a built-in coordinator agent.

roles.answer: Roles are conventions (aliases like lead/reviewer); ORCH assigns task/worker.

model_harness_effort.answer: agent start --kind chooses harness; model and effort are the agent's own settings; automation access chooses native flags.

messages.answer: agent prompt pastes and submits text into another agent's input; agent keys answers prompts.

results_return.answer: agent read returns output; agent prompt --wait blocks until settle; workers can prompt the lead back.

cross_harness.answer: Any detected agent kind can be targeted by any other.

orchestration_owner.answer: Luvus ships the delegation commands, skill and ORCH; the coordinator itself is a user-run agent.

activation.answer: Commands work without configuration; luvus skill enable adds the skill; no experimental flag.

authentication.answer: Pane env injects socket path and pane id; local OS user trust.

live_progress.answer: Sidebar state, agent list and live pane view show child progress.

retained_results.answer: Results persist as retained scrollback and ORCH notes/output; scrollback is bounded (10 MiB default).

followup.answer: Prompt the same pane again or resume its session.

invocation.answer: luvus agent verbs, =name shorthand, ORCH task start.

limitations: Delegation is pasted prompts and screen reads, not structured messages; no automatic role assignment.

claims.answer: Beta automations run on one-time, interval, daily or weekly schedules from the detached server (TUI can be closed), starting a fresh ORCH worker or prompting an existing agent, with misfire/overlap policies and bounded history; no event triggers and no automatic retries; stopping the server stops the scheduler.

schedules.answer: Once, interval (≥60s), daily and weekly with IANA timezone.

events.answer: Docs state automations are time-triggered and dependencies do not trigger them.

recurring_tasks.answer: Each due occurrence creates a fresh ORCH task.

completion_conditions.answer: Run history and task gate record result; active-agent delivery is only recorded as delivered.

scheduler_location.answer: Detached Luvus server caches the nearest UTC deadline.

retries.answer: No automatic retry of a failed agent run.

client_independence.answer: Closing the TUI does not pause automations; stopping the server does.

limitations: Time triggers only; BETA; no retries; owning server must be running.

claims.answer: Humans can steer in any pane, answer blocked prompts, stop or close panes, release tasks and resume agent sessions; blocked state surfaces in the sidebar with optional sound; ORCH marks automation tasks blocked on unknown prompts without auto-approving. No pause primitive and no push notifications.

pause.answer: Bounded search of docs and CLI help finds no pause command for running agents.

stop.answer: task release, pane close, agent keys ctrl+c; server stop ends PTYs.

resume.answer: Agent session resume and task retry.

steer.answer: Type in the pane, Commander, agent prompt.

notifications.answer: Optional done/blocked sounds and sidebar state; no remote push.

pending_decisions.answer: Blocked agents shown red when a permission prompt is on screen; Mission Control a to answer.

escalation.answer: ORCH marks scheduled tasks blocked and records the detected prompt.

visible_errors.answer: Gate output, merge conflicts and automation failures are shown on tasks and runs.

chat_terminal_parity.answer: The pane is the agent's real terminal, so CLI questions appear as they do natively.

retained_history.answer: Scrollback bounded (10 MiB default); resume reopens agent conversation.

limitations: No pause/resume of a running agent beyond the agent's own controls; notifications are local sounds, not push.

claims.answer: The ◇ orch board lists every task with status, id, title, dependencies, mode and worker location plus leases; the sidebar lists agents with states across workspaces; Mission Control shows agents, tokens, cost and context. No parent/child tree or epic grouping; attention is shown by blocked state.

fleet_fixture.answer: This catalog does not run products, so no multi-epic fixture was exercised.

attention.answer: Blocked rows and blocked agents surface needs-input; review rows show failed gates.

history.answer: Run history for automations and previous attempts for tasks.

workload.answer: Mission Control summarizes agents, tokens, cost, context.

navigation_errors.answer: Enter/double click jumps to the worker pane; gate output visible on the task.

fixture_mode.answer: No fixture or demo mode documented; not tested.

limitations: No epics or hierarchy view; fleet visualization is a table and sidebar.
claims.unknownReason: Catalog does not run products; fixture behavior is untested rather than missing.

claims.answer: No mandatory workflow: start any agent in a pane or use the board; Manual/Now start, worktree vs workspace mode, access level and schedule are chosen per task/automation. Agent model/effort are agent settings. The UI shows workers, leases and run history; natural-language configuration is whatever the user's agent does through the skill.

quick_task.answer: Start an agent in a pane immediately, or task Now start.

presets.answer: Bounded search finds no workflow presets beyond key/theme presets.

natural_language.answer: Agents with the luvus skill can operate Luvus from natural-language requests.

agent_configuration.answer: Agent choice per task; model and effort are agent settings.

in_run_changes.answer: Steer in pane or via prompt; task prompt locked after start.

live_roles.answer: Aliases and ORCH worker labels show who is who.

discoverability.answer: Ctrl+Space ? lists shortcuts; luvus help all; docs site.

auth_friction.answer: Local trust; agents must be logged in; sandboxed agents may need socket approval.

limitations: No presets or role templates; coordinator and child roles are not modeled beyond aliases and tasks.

claims.answer: Execution is local by default; the same server can run on an SSH-reachable machine you own (luvus --remote or saved machines) where panes keep running after the client disconnects and another device can attach, or a hosted bridge-free SSH app on a phone. Luvus operates no cloud; sleep or shutdown of the host stops execution.

local.answer: Server and PTYs run on the local machine.

byo_remote.answer: luvus --remote host and saved Remote Machine profiles attach to a server on your own host.

self_hosted.answer: The server is local software on any host you run; no separate control plane.

hybrid.answer: Local and remote workspaces sit side by side in one TUI.

provisioning.answer: Setup can install the binary on the remote host over SSH with approval; host provisioning is the user's.

payer.answer: The user pays for their own hosts and agent subscriptions.

resources.answer: Resources are the host's; Luvus imposes none.

region.answer: Region depends on the user's host.

expiry.answer: No expiry; server lives until stopped or the host reboots.

client_disconnect.answer: Detaching or closing a client leaves server and PTYs running; Luvus Web closing does not stop panes.

other_device_continuation.answer: Reattach with luvus --remote, SSH, or a browser bridge from another device.

limitations: No vendor cloud; durability depends on the user's host staying up and (on Windows) restarts.
claims.unknownReason: Region and compute sizing belong to the user's own host.

claims.answer: Isolation is worktree-based or none: ORCH worktree mode gives each worker its own Git worktree and branch with merge in a separate integration worktree; workspace mode intentionally shares one checkout. Panes run as the OS user; there are no container or VM options and no network or secret boundaries beyond the agent's own sandbox flags.

checkout.answer: Workspace mode shares the existing checkout.

worktree.answer: First-class worktree workspaces; module providers possible.

container.answer: Bounded search of src and docs for docker/podman/container finds no isolation feature.

vm.answer: No VM isolation in the pinned release.

os_sandbox.answer: Only via the agent's native per-run flags (e.g. codex --sandbox read-only); not Luvus-enforced.

filesystem.answer: Worktrees separate files; panes can access the user's whole account.

secrets.answer: No secret injection or boundary; agents use the user's environment.

code_separation.answer: Merges happen in a dedicated integration worktree so the user's checkout is untouched.

security_boundary.answer: Docs describe a single-user local-trust tool and do not claim hostile-code containment.

limitations: Worktrees are not a security sandbox; access profiles rely on each agent's native flags.

claims.answer: Client detach never stops work; if the server dies (reboot, restart) Luvus saves layout and screens and the next server restores workspaces, tabs, cwd, last screen and resumes supported agent sessions natively (shells restart fresh); orch ledger persists; active workers from a previous server lifetime are recorded as failed. No expiry.

client_disconnect.answer: Panes keep running; reattach shows live state.

worker_crash.answer: A crashed pane/agent is detected; ORCH retry creates a new attempt keeping the old record.

service_restart.answer: Session snapshot restored and agent conversations resumed.

transcript_reload.answer: Resume reopens agent conversations; saved pane screens optional.

process_reconnect.answer: Live processes cannot outlive the server; shells restart.

task_resume.answer: Tasks persist; running workers become failed on server loss and are retried.

state_reconstruction.answer: Layout, cwd, last screen and agent sessions rebuilt.

context_loss.answer: Agent-side context returns via native resume where supported; shells and unsupported agents start fresh.

duplicate_actions.answer: Automations avoid double launch by persisted occurrence keys; uncertain dispatch fails rather than replays.

manual_repair.answer: luvus server restart; doctor; automation rebind.

multi_day_continuity.answer: Server keeps panes alive until host reboot; after reboot resume restores agents natively.

limitations: worker_crash: A crashed pane/agent is detected; ORCH retry creates a new attempt keeping the old record.
task_resume: Tasks persist; running workers become failed on server loss and are retried.
context_loss: Agent-side context returns via native resume where supported; shells and unsupported agents start fresh.

claims.answer: Luvus does not manage dependencies, caches, services, ports or secrets for workspaces; worktrees start from Git state and the user or agent installs dependencies. A module worktree provider can run custom creation scripts. Pane environments inject LUVUS_PANE_ID and socket path.

dependencies.answer: Bounded search finds no dependency installer; a worktree provider module can run setup.

snapshots.answer: No environment snapshots (only session layout snapshots).

ports.answer: No port allocation (web bridge default 4174 only).

duplicate_installs.answer: Each worktree installs separately unless the user's tooling shares caches.

collisions.answer: No collision handling for services or ports.

remote_setup.answer: Remote binary install is managed; project setup is manual.

limitations: No automatic dependency, cache, service, port or secret management.

claims.answer: Luvus enforces few limits: a 85% context gate blocks marking a task done until compaction, a quality gate must pass, automation prompts are bounded (32 KiB) with misfire grace and at least 60 s intervals, and agent-pane limits follow the agents. No time, turn, token or spend budgets, and no automatic retries.

time_limits.answer: No task timeouts except agent prompt --wait --timeout and gate cancellation on release.

token_limits.answer: Context usage gate at 85% blocks done; no token budget.

spend_limits.answer: Bounded search of orch/automation/mission for budget or spend limits finds none; cost is display-only.

timeouts.answer: agent prompt --wait defaults to 300 s (exit 2); gates run in contained processes.

retries.answer: task retry is manual; automations do not retry.

provider_failures.answer: Provider failures appear only in the agent's pane.

enforcement.answer: Context gate and quality gate are enforced; display values are not.

limitations: No spend, token, time or turn limits; the context gate depends on the worker reporting heartbeat.

claims.answer: Luvus shows live per-agent state, Mission Control tables with tokens, context use and cost, automation run history and health, task output/notes and structured runtime logs that omit pane content. Usage comes from each agent's own store and shows — when unknown; there are no exports, per-project or time series statistics.

logs.answer: Server/client logs under ~/.luvus/logs that exclude pane output and prompts; panes show agent logs.

failure_reasons.answer: Gate output, merge conflict status and automation run failure reasons are recorded.

usage_export.answer: luvus mission snapshot / UHP mission.snapshot return usage JSON; no file export format.

task_stats.answer: Per-task context heartbeat and attempt times.

agent_stats.answer: Mission Control per-session tokens, context, cost, model.

project_stats.answer: No per-project totals beyond workspace filters.

session_cost.answer: Mission Control cost per agent session.

tokens.answer: Input, output, cache tokens and context use.

drilldown.answer: Selected Agent panel and session rows.

limitations: Several agents report no usage; no per-task cost, alerts or export.

claims.answer: Leases prevent overlapping path work, only one task merges at a time, gates run in contained process trees and are cancelled on release, and Luvus avoids per-agent polling; there are no CPU/RAM limits, queues for checks, throttling or per-host resource scheduling.

concurrency.answer: No global concurrency limit; per-project lease conflicts.

bounded_tests.answer: Gate runs one command per task in a contained process tree.

recovery.answer: Interrupted integration restores prior state after restart.

limitations: No resource-aware scheduling, check reuse or backpressure.

claims.answer: Single-user local tool. Luvus Web can pair up to eight of your own browsers or devices to the same session, read-only by default or with control, and several TUI clients attach at once, each with its own viewport; there is no multi-user identity, comments, presence or ordering rules.

visibility.answer: Paired browsers and attached TUIs see the same panes.

comments.answer: DIFF notes are local and private to the user.

presence.answer: No presence indicators; Devices panel lists paired browsers.

coprompting.answer: Several paired control browsers or clients can type into a pane with no ordering or attribution.

ordering.answer: No input ordering or lock between clients documented.

conflicts.answer: No conflict handling beyond PTY input.

permissions.answer: Read-only vs control authority per bridge; device cap 1–8.

owner_online.answer: The owner's server (and bridge process) must be running.

limitations: No user identities, comments, presence or conflict handling; shared devices all act as the same owner.

organization_roles.answer: Bounded search of src, web and docs (terms role, sso, oidc, saml, scim, member) finds no such feature.

project_roles.answer: Bounded search of src, web and docs (terms role, sso, oidc, saml, scim, member) finds no such feature.

provisioning.answer: Bounded search of src, web and docs (terms role, sso, oidc, saml, scim, member) finds no such feature.

claims.answer: Luvus does not approve tool or command calls itself: blocked prompts of the agent are shown and can be answered by the user through the pane or agent keys; automations never type approvals and map access levels to the agent's native flags. command.answer: Agent permission prompts are detected and shown blocked; answered in the pane.

delivery.answer: No delivery approvals; DIFF has no publish action.

lifetime.answer: Web/UHP access authority expires or ends with the bridge process.

allow.answer: User answers in pane; agent keys can answer prompts.

revoke.answer: Stopping the bridge revokes authority; disabling a skill removes it.

tunnels.answer: Bridge authority is process-bound; Ctrl+C revokes.

defaults.answer: Web read-only by default; automations default to workspace access; Luvus never changes agent permanent config.

safer_modes.answer: Read-only/workspace/full access for scheduled work via native flags.

enforcement.answer: Access limits enforced by the agent's flags; Luvus refuses unsupported combinations.

limitations: No product-enforced command/network/secret policy; approvals are the agent's.

claims.answer: Luvus keeps task notes, outputs, automation run history, the event stream (luvus events, not persisted as a log) and diagnostics logs that exclude pane content; the session is single-user so actions carry no identities. No audit trail, export or integrity model.

actions.answer: Events bus for task and automation actions; not persisted.

approvals.answer: Approvals are not recorded by Luvus.

export.answer: No export feature beyond reading JSON files.

limitations: No audit with retention/integrity; events are streams, not stored.

claims.answer: A native read-only DIFF surface lists staged, worktree, untracked and conflicted files, shows split/stack diffs with search, hunk and file navigation, viewed marks and local notes that can be sent to a live agent; the Git tab shows PR details and approve; keyboard-first and mobile-friendly. pending_reviews.answer: DIFF filters Unviewed/Changed/Notes; Git tab lists PRs with checks.

change_understanding.answer: Diff view plus hunk explanation; no summaries.

missed_evidence.answer: Unviewed filter marks files not yet reviewed.

narrow_screen.answer: Auto layout falls back to stack on narrow viewports; mobile mode.

context_switching.answer: Notes persist locally keyed by repo/worktree.

retained_context.answer: Notes and viewed fingerprints stored in the owner-only state root.

limitations: No guided review queue, request changes or shipping guidance; notes are local.

claims.answer: Anyone with access to the same server (SSH account, paired browser) can attach to the same live panes with identical session history and runtime, including after the original client disconnects; ownership is the OS user so there is no distinct person transfer or attribution. ongoing_takeover.answer: A new client attaches to the running server.

artifacts.answer: Files and worktrees on the host.

context_loss.answer: Server loss still restores via resume.

harness_transfer.answer: No transfer of one agent conversation to another harness.

limitations: Single-user model: no separate identities, permissions or attribution; harness transfer not supported.

claims.answer: Luvus retains task output and notes, worktrees and branches, DIFF views of current Git layers and scrollback; there is no artifact gallery, screenshot/recording capture or test-report store. Mermaid/Markdown previews are native; web uploads reach the server as files.

diffs.answer: DIFF and git tab diffs for live Git state.

documents.answer: Markdown and Mermaid preview of files.

test_outputs.answer: Gate output stored on the task.

reviewer_outputs.answer: Reviewer agent output stays in its pane.

child_findings.answer: Read via agent read while scrollback lasts.

claims.answer: ORCH tasks can carry a quality-gate command that must pass before a task is done and can merge; failed gates hold the task in review; the context gate blocks done above 85%. lint.answer: Any command can be the gate.

types.answer: Any command can be the gate.

claims.answer: Luvus creates worktrees and branches, merges finished worker branches into luvus/integration in an isolated worktree with clean conflict abort, shows commits/branches/PRs through git and gh and starts gh pr create in a pane. commits.answer: Commits shown; creation is by agents.

pull_requests.answer: gh pr create launched in a pane; PR detail view.

comments.answer: PR discussion readable; DIFF notes local.

ci_response.answer: Red checks notify; no automated response.

conflicts.answer: Merge conflict aborts and marks task blocked.

limitations: No product-managed commits, rebase, PR review comments or CI-response automation.

claims.answer: Approval is by the user: the gate pass plus pressing m merges a task branch into luvus/integration (a Luvus-owned branch, never the user's branch); PR approve through gh from PR detail; no release or deployment features and no exact-revision binding of approvals.

approve.answer: PR detail a approves via gh.

claims.answer: Task records branch, worktree and exact integration commit after merge, previous attempts and gate output; retry creates a new attempt without deleting history; no PR/build/deployment links, rollback or revert feature, or stale-approval invalidation.

claims.answer: Entire Luvus (server, TUI, web client, docs) is in one public repository under Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, Cargo.toml); vendored alacritty_terminal and vte keep their own licenses. There is no hosted extension or closed component.

evidence.finding: Package luvus 0.14.3, Rust 1.88, license Apache-2.0, repository RizRiyz/luvus, ratatui terminal UI; no GUI toolkit.

evidence.title: Update checker source
evidence.finding: Update check fetches https://luvus.dev/latest.json; config.check_updates (src/config.rs line 68, default true) disables it.

evidence.title: Git tab actions source
evidence.finding: Git tab PR list runs gh pr create in a pane; PR detail approve/check out use gh; the product does not create PRs through its own API.

evidence.title: Model pricing table source
evidence.finding: Built-in per-model pricing used by Mission Control to estimate cost when the agent store records none.

evidence.title: Agent registry source
evidence.finding: One compiled-in descriptor per agent (aider, amp, antigravity, arc_studio, claude, codex, copilot, cursor, devin, droid, fx, gemini, grok, hermes, kilo, kimi, kiro, letta, muse, omp, opencode, pi, qwen) declaring identity, resume, fork and optional integration.

evidence.title: Codex unattended profile source
evidence.finding: Codex automation access maps read-only to --sandbox read-only and full to --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox: native per-run flags, not a Luvus sandbox.

evidence.title: Web UHP client package
evidence.finding: Internal TypeScript UHP client used by the browser app and bridge (web/packages/app, web/bridge); private, not published as an SDK.

evidence.title: Release workflow
evidence.finding: GitHub Actions builds per-target binaries and packages (tar.gz, zip, deb, rpm) for release assets.

evidence.title: Writing modules: Agent Ping example
evidence.finding: Docs show an example module (examples/modules/agent-ping) that posts a webhook when an agent goes blocked or finishes; the webhook URL is a secret module setting. It is module code, not a built-in Luvus feature.
